newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Polaris II venture fund raises $40 mln.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Polaris II venture fund raises $40 mln.

text.p: The Polaris II venture capital fund has raised another $40 million from foreign investors, bringing total capital to $124 million, its parent Dovrat Shrem and Co said on Sunday.

A spokesman declined to identify the investors but said they were mainly U.S. pension funds and other tax-exempt institutions. He added that with the latest round of financing, the fund was now Israel's biggest and fully subscribed.
Dovrat Shrem said the investors would put the money into the fund as it was needed.
It said the fund would charge a management fee of 2.25 percent.
Dovrat, a Tel Aviv-based investment bank, said Polaris II would be investing in companies in telecommunications, software, advanced medical technologies, electronics and biotechnology.

Polaris II was formed by Dovrat Shrem together with the U.S. investment bank Cowen and Co and the Travelers insurance group. Other investors include BEA, a U.S. fund-management company, and Claridge Israel, an investment company controlled by Charles Bronfman.
Dovrat Shrem's first Polaris fund manages $20 million.
